headlines.title: 한경협 “ 고용 의 71 %는 서비스업 … 지원법 마련 시급”

key_headlines.title: Energy Stability Measures Total Mobilization Amid US-Iran Conflict
key_headlines.summary: The government is deploying all measures, including releasing reserves and securing additional crude oil, to ensure energy stability as the Middle East crisis escalates. The crisis management level has been upgraded, and coal power plant limits are lifted, alongside stricter management of gas stations.

key_headlines.title: Won-Dollar Exchange Rate Surpasses 1500 Won, First Time in 17 Years
key_headlines.summary: The Korean Won depreciated past 1500 won against the dollar for the first time in 17 years during intraday trading, triggered by soaring international oil prices following US airstrikes on Iran's oil export facilities. The exchange rate opened at 1501 won, marking the third major currency crisis wave since the financial crisis.

key_headlines.title: IEA Initiates Emergency Oil Release; South Korea Prepares
key_headlines.summary: As the Middle East crisis worsens, with risks of a Strait of Hormuz blockade due to the US-Iran conflict, International Energy Agency (IEA) member countries have begun releasing emergency oil reserves. South Korea is actively reviewing its specific release methods, timing, and volume, preparing to release 22.46 million barrels.

key_headlines.title: Exchange Rate Opens Above 1500 Won, Highest Since Financial Crisis
key_headlines.summary: The Won-Dollar exchange rate opened at 1501.0 won, up 7.3 won from the previous week's close, marking the first time since March 10, 2009, during the global financial crisis, that the opening rate surpassed 1500 won. This surge also pushed 3-year Treasury bond yields to a 21-month high, prompting the government to consider Treasury buybacks.

key_headlines.title: Government Mobilizes Crisis Response Team Amid Middle East Escalation
key_headlines.summary: The government and ruling party held their second Economic Response Task Force meeting for the Middle East situation, upgrading the crisis management level to 'caution.' Measures include releasing national oil reserves, securing additional crude, and easing restrictions on coal power generation to preemptively manage energy supply and stabilize markets.

sections.Hot Economy News: The US-Iran conflict is severely impacting Korea's economy, leading to the won-dollar exchange rate surpassing 1500 won for the first time in 17 years and a significant increase in international oil prices. In response, the government is activating all energy stability measures, including releasing strategic oil reserves, securing additional crude oil, and lifting restrictions on coal power generation. The International Energy Agency (IEA) has also begun emergency oil releases, with South Korea preparing its own detailed plans. Financial authorities are intensifying oversight of fuel stations and considering emergency Treasury buybacks to stabilize markets amidst rising bond yields. This situation marks the third major economic wave since the financial crisis, prompting heightened alert from policymakers.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Economists predict that a sustained rise in international oil prices to $140 per barrel due to the US-Iran war could push global inflation to 5.8% and bring the US economy close to recession, necessitating 0.5% interest rate hikes by major central banks. While South Korea's inflation and unemployment rates currently compare favorably to the US, the oil price surge poses a significant burden. China is also expected to face challenges, with its producer price index signaling a potential negative GDP deflator for the first quarter. Regionally, Daegu and Gyeongbuk experienced a decline in employment and a rise in unemployment during January.
sections.Financial Markets: The surge in international oil prices and the won-dollar exchange rate surpassing 1500 won are creating significant headwinds for the Korean stock market, primarily by increasing raw material import costs and threatening corporate profits. Despite these pressures, the Kospi index managed to open higher, buoyed by strong performance in the semiconductor sector. However, the bond market is also under stress, with 3-year Treasury bond yields reaching a 21-month high, prompting the Bank of Korea to conduct a record 3 trillion won bond purchase to stabilize rates. The government and ruling party are prepared for emergency Treasury buybacks if market conditions worsen. Analysts anticipate continued market volatility, influenced by the escalating US-Iran conflict and upcoming US Federal Open Market Committee decisions.
sections.Industry & Technology: Amidst general market trends, specific sectors like semiconductors, defense, and aerospace are seeing individual stocks reach new highs, alongside notable gains in the biotechnology and nuclear power industries. However, the electric vehicle battery and petrochemical sectors are facing headwinds, leading SKC to announce voluntary redundancies for employees hired before 2025. This move aims to improve cost structures and enhance organizational efficiency in response to a prolonged industry downturn. The company is offering 50% of annual salary as severance pay, with final approvals and departure dates yet to be determined.
sections.Real Estate: The supply of new apartments, particularly those from urban redevelopment and reconstruction projects in Seoul, has significantly declined in recent years due to tight real estate project financing and rising interest rates. While Seoul's home price increase slowed in February compared to January, there is an observable increase in listing of properties for sale and potential downward pressure on prices in some areas. A notable trend shows a majority of new apartment offerings nationwide are priced above surrounding market rates, causing some young individuals to cancel their subscription savings accounts. Singapore's housing policy, which strategically increases supply during periods of sharp price appreciation, is being considered as a valuable benchmark for addressing South Korea's housing challenges.
sections.International Economy: Major central banks, including the US Federal Reserve, ECB, and BOJ, are bracing for a "super week" of interest rate decisions amidst global high oil prices, with the Fed widely expected to maintain its current rates. Former US President Donald Trump continues his push for "absolute authority" on tariffs, advocating for a 10% global tariff on all trading partners and criticizing the Supreme Court for obstructing his efforts. Meanwhile, as the US focuses on the escalating conflict with Iran, China is actively strengthening its security and public order alliances with Vietnam through an unprecedented "3+3" strategic dialogue. China's crude oil imports have significantly increased, with much of it directed to strategic reserves, indicating a strategic shift amid regional tensions.
sections.AI & Economy: The Ministry of SMEs and Startups is committed to boosting sales for small businesses by fostering local entrepreneurs and expanding digital education, including AI training, to enhance the competitiveness of the entire small business ecosystem. In the biotech sector, SyntekaBio is projected for significant growth, leveraging its AI-powered drug discovery platform to efficiently identify effective drug candidates and generate high added value. Telecommunication companies are rapidly accelerating their AI transformation (AX) initiatives, aiming to establish a "one person, one AI agent" system to boost employee productivity and expand into new revenue streams beyond traditional services. Nobel laureate economists warn that if South Korea fears failure in embracing AI, it risks failing in its future economic planning.
sections.Others: The Blue House is responding cautiously to the US request for South Korea to dispatch warships to the Strait of Hormuz, emphasizing close communication with the US on this sensitive issue. Experts suggest that any operation to secure the Strait of Hormuz would require substantial military forces, including ground troops, and a protracted commitment. The US-Iran conflict is anticipated to last for several more weeks, with potential military targets extending to Iran's critical Kharg Island oil export facilities, heightening concerns about prolonged warfare and its global economic impact. Starting in April, international flight fuel surcharges are projected to more than triple due to rising oil prices and exchange rates, with further increases expected in May. Separately, an employer who accrued 500 million won in unpaid wages and severance over a decade was arrested after years of evading authorities abroad.
